title: Giants select Barry Bonds’ nephew in third round of MLB Draft
content:
With the 90th pick in the 2026 MLB Draft, the San Francisco Giants selected Rutgers outfielder Peyton Bonds in the third round. The 20-year-old sophomore hit .352 for the Scarlet Knights last season, and he projects to be a plus center fielder, but you’re not reading this for his scouting report. You’re reading this because he’s the nephew of Barry Bonds and grandson of Bobby Bonds, two baseball legends.

More specifically, those are two Giants legends, with the two Bondses combining for almost 3,000 games in a Giants uniform and 14 All-Star Games. While there’s no such thing as a grand-godson, you might as well add Willie Mays (Barry’s godfather) into the lineage. This is a player who grew up thinking Giants thoughts his entire life, joining the organization that makes for the most interesting pairing of this year’s draft.

Don’t let the name deceive you, though. The youngest Bonds wasn’t raised by a baseball superstar, but by Bobby Bonds Jr., who spent seven seasons in the minors and another five after that playing in the independent Atlantic League. That’s a grinder’s path, not a superstar’s path, and it’s easy to think those lessons will be just as valuable for a third-round pick as anything he could have gleaned from his more famous uncle.

Still, the Giants will have a Bonds in the organization again, as they did in the 1970s, 1990s and 2000s. (They also drafted Barry out of high school in 1982, but he didn’t sign, if you need more decade continuity.) The odds are against most prospects drafted outside the first round, but the Giants and their fans will be following this one closely for understandable reasons.
